title: Senate concludes P7.2-T proposed 2027 budget deliberations
summary: In a news release posted on its Facebook page, the upper chamber announced it finished marathon deliberations on next year"s budget “after days of rigorous plenary debate.”

blocks.text: The Senate on Saturday wrapped up its deliberations on the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027.
In a news release posted on its Facebook page, the upper chamber announced it had finished marathon deliberations on next year’s budget “after days of rigorous plenary debate.”
During its deliberations, the Senate said it advanced the proposed budgets of major government institutions, namely:

items: Congress of the Philippines - P27.89 billion
Department of National Defense - P326.9 billion
Department of Public Works and Highways - P587.9 billion
Commission on Higher Education (CHED) - P38.821 billion
Department of Migrant Workers - P11.894 billion

blocks.text: The Senate added its deliberations also covered peace, social, and regional development offices, including the Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity (OPAPRU) at P9.304 billion; National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) at P1.738 billion; Marawi Compensation Board (MCB) at P1.247 billion; National Amnesty Commission (NAC) at P266.6 million; Commission on Filipinos Overseas (CFO) at P187.8 million; and Metropolitan Baguio City, La Trinidad, Itogon, Sablan, Tuba, and Tublay Development Authority (MBLISTTDA) at P45.4 million.

The upper chamber said it took up the proposed allocations of other executive offices, including the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) at P8.514 billion; National Intelligence Coordinating Agency (NICA) at P3.086 billion; National Security Council (NSC) at P1.122 billion; Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) at P335 million; Film Development Council of the Philippines (FDCP) at P311 million; Philippine Racing Commission (Philracom) at P202.8 million; Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB) at P69.742 million; Optical Media Board (OMB) at P53.462 million; and other agencies. —VAL, GMA News
